description: The bar chart illustrates the perplexity of a language model under different pruning percentages (ranging from 10% to 80%) using two distinct pruning strategies: “Per-Output” (blue bars) and “Per-Layer” (orange bars), as evaluated in the context of DLP (Dynamic Layerwise Pruning) for large language models. The horizontal axis displays the pruning percentage in 10% increments, while the vertical axis represents perplexity on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10¹ to 10³. At lower pruning rates (10%–50%), both methods yield similar and relatively low perplexity values, mostly below 10¹. As pruning increases beyond 60%, perplexity rises sharply for both strategies, with the “Per-Layer” method consistently showing higher perplexity than “Per-Output” at each pruning level. At 80% pruning, the “Per-Output” method achieves a perplexity of approximately 500, while “Per-Layer” reaches nearly 1000, indicating a more severe degradation in model performance under layer-wise pruning. The bars are grouped by pruning percentage, with each group containing two adjacent bars for direct comparison, and the legend clearly identifies the color coding for each pruning strategy. The chart visually emphasizes the growing performance gap between the two methods as pruning intensity increases.
